subject: Next steps: deployment-mode clarification for SmallBank (latency & throughput)

Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>

Subject: Next steps: deployment-mode clarification for SmallBank (latency & throughput)

Thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap from our discovery and the follow-ups we agreed on. I kept it focused so we can pick next steps quickly.

Key latency/throughput signals you shared (from call):
- Steady-state QPS: ~100 requests/sec for customer-facing fraud checks
- SLO target: p95 <= 50ms end-to-end (including network) for the critical path
- Burst profile: up to ~500 QPS for short bursts (5-10 minutes), traffic tied to batch settlement windows
- Data residency: US-only; sensitive PII is processed but not stored long-term

Options we discussed and what we need to choose between them:
1) Hosted API (Redwood hosted): fastest onboarding, autoscaling to handle bursts, built-in caching and continuous batching. Potential trade: multi-tenant endpoint unless you take a Dedicated pool.
2) Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool): predictable throughput and isolation, can hit tighter tail latencies under consistent load, recommended if you want steady-state cost predictability and more control over model variants.
3) Private VPC / on-prem: for full network isolation and compliance; longer lead time and ops footprint.

Clarifying asks for you (quick, one-line replies are perfect):
- Confirm the p95 SLO must be 50ms including network, or if 50ms is the server-side p95 target (excluding client network).
- For bursts: how long are typical bursts (minutes/hours)? is 10 minutes a good worst-case?
- Any procurement/contract constraints (PO process, security review timeline) that would make Hosted infeasible within 6–8 weeks?

Proposed next steps from our side:
- I’ll draft a short SLA/comparison that maps your signals to likely deployment recommendations and cost bands (Hosted vs Dedicated). Attached a one-page matrix and a network note for the team.
- If you want, we can schedule a technical deep-dive with Neha (architect) to walk the tail-latency tuning and KV-cache/ batching strategies. 45 minutes should be enough.

Attachments: [Attachment: SLA-comparison-table.xlsx (spreadsheet, 24KB)], [Attachment: network-architecture-notes.pdf (pdf, 180KB)]

Thanks — I’ll wait for the clarifying bullets and we’ll propose a pilot plan.

—

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Quick answers below:
- The 50ms p95 is our end-to-end target; if the server-side p95 is 40ms that gives us a little headroom, but the overall must be <= 50ms.
- Bursts: usually tied to batch settlement windows, avg 6–8 minutes but we’ve seen up to ~12 minutes during end-of-day.
- Procurement: we can do Hosted in the short term; procurement requires a standard SaaS addendum and an InfoSec review (SOC2 + encryption at rest). Dedicated is fine but will need budget sign-off from procurement (longer lead time).

One more detail: request payload sizes vary — typical 1–2 KB, but some enriched requests with context reach ~10KB. We care about tail latency much more than nominal throughput.

Would be great to see the SLA matrix you mentioned. If Hosted can demonstrate 40ms server p95 under our burst profile with autoscaling, that might be ideal to start.

Sam Patel
Head of Platform, SmallBank Financial Services
sam.patel@smallbank.com

Subject: Re: Next steps: deployment-mode clarification for SmallBank (latency & throughput)

Appreciate the quick details — very helpful. Short replies to each point and a suggested pilot: 

Latency targets
- We’ll treat your 50ms as end-to-end. For Hosted, we’ll aim for server-side p95 <= 35–40ms to give you buffer for network variance. For Dedicated we can tighten further depending on the instance profile and model quantization.

Burst handling
- Autoscaling on Hosted can handle 500 QPS bursts for 10–12 minutes; we’ll provision burst headroom during the pilot and exercise the autoscaler to validate spin-up times. For stricter tail needs, Dedicated with pre-warmed pools reduces variance.

Payload sizes and batching
- We’ll tune batching to message size and latency targets (smaller batches at low-latency SLOs). KV/prefix caching will reduce repeated context costs.

Recommended pilot (3 weeks):
1) Hosted pilot with dedicated endpoint config (single-tenant logical endpoint) — validates autoscaling and p95 under your burst profile.
2) Run synthetic burst tests (we can supply a load harness) and 2–3 days of shadow traffic routing from production.
3) If results show p95 variance > 10ms from target, we’ll propose a Dedicated capacity proof-of-concept (short reserved pool for benchmarking).

I attached the SLA/comparison matrix and network notes to this thread — highlights are in the first tab. If that looks reasonable, propose we schedule the 45-minute technical deep-dive next Tue or Wed.

Next actions:
- Sam/Priya: confirm deep-dive day/time preference and whether you want us to run initial synthetic tests on your behalf or share the load harness for you to run.
- I’ll loop in our engineering delivery lead if you confirm the pilot.

Thanks,
Marissa

Quick technical note from the infra side — thanks for including me. Two points to call out before the deep-dive: 
1) Network egress/domains: if you run Hosted and must whitelist IPs, we’ll provide a CIDR range and pre-warm NAT gateways to avoid cold-path network variability.
2) Encryption & audit: Hosted supports customer-managed keys (KMS) and detailed access logs; if your InfoSec needs HSM-backed keys we’ll map the certificate flow. Private VPC/on-prem will change the timeline by ~6–8 weeks.

I can run the deep-dive technical session next Wed 10:00–10:45 PT and bring the SRE who owns autoscaling behavior. If that works for SmallBank, mark it and I’ll add a calendar invite + agenda.

—
